v1.initial_review: Metadata projection, checkpoint order, cleanup guards, and CLI/artifact wiring were reviewed without a proven serious problem in those areas. Supplemental review of the authoritative menu constructor subsequently found the shared API-key identifier mismatch below.

finding.actual_contract: A shared API key has current.kind=shared and id=apikey:<key UUID>:<model>. Pooled subscriptions instead remain kind=subscription with a binding UUID.
finding.v1_mismatch: The v1 projection allowed the composite ID only for kind=apiKey and required a UUID for kind=shared.
finding.effect: A legitimate explicit shared API-key selection is rejected with recovery_metadata_invalid before the case creates its temporary profile or changes its model.
finding.required_fix: Use the composite API-key ID validator for both apiKey and shared, preserving the original primitive fields.
finding.disposition: Resolved in the final candidate; retained in this record. V1 is not approved.

facts: Hosted uses HOSTED_CHOICE, empty modelId, and provider=mikka.
Own and pooled subscription options use row.bindingId; subscription current uses option.bindingId or binding.bindingId and kind=subscription.
Both own and shared API-key current IDs are generated by apiKeyOptionId; kind is apiKey when key.mine and shared otherwise.
modelId and provider are supplied by the actual binding or key; chosen is copied from the resolver choice.chosen.
Credential labels, account labels, owner display names and quota objects are separate fields and are not recovery fields.
HOSTED_CHOICE is the nil UUID.
apiKeyOptionId composes apikey:<keyId>:<model>; parseApiKeyOption splits the UUID-shaped key component and model suffix.
The four menu kinds are hosted, subscription, apiKey, and shared; modelId/provider/id are strings and chosen is boolean.
Ordinary PUT accepts the menu id through a strict object with a bounded nonempty string.
Temporary selection requires UUID bot and UUID id.
Implicit restoration requires a UUID bindingId and a decimal revision string of length 1 through 10.
The route returns the real setTemporaryBotModel receipt and delegates normal choices to chooseBotModel.
Ordinary non-hosted subscription choices validate a UUID binding.
Temporary selection returns the actual stored bindingId and xmin revision only after commit.
Implicit restoration matches owner, workspace, bot, bindingId, xmin, and absence of API-key fields; it does not infer a receipt from equal menu values.
Bot-scoped binding clones use a UUID-shaped deterministic identifier.
Subscription menu rows source bindingId from the binding record id, not from a display label or catalogue model string.
Actual API-key provider values are anthropic, openai, deepseek, kimi, or custom; all satisfy the recovery provider identifier validator.
API-key model strings are trimmed, nonempty, and bounded to 128 characters but do not have the recovery journal's ASCII character allowlist.
Saving an API-key choice validates its UUID key ID and verifies the model belongs to a currently usable key.
The journal character validator is deliberately narrower than the product API contract; full arbitrary-model-string compatibility is not claimed.

original_tests.verification: The complete original UTF-8 file is an exact contiguous byte sequence after the five new imports in both v1 and the reviewed final candidate. No original test declaration, body, fixture, assertion or loop case was changed.
original_tests.loop_expansion: Two declarations each register once for each of five profileGet404s entries, adding eight registrations.

retained_source_guards: The original ownRunsStopped gate still controls profile archiving and model restoration.
The original ownerIdle inventory gates remain on preparation and restoration.
Original Profile version/digest and full in-memory definition comparisons remain before restoration.
The explicit model restoration compares original and last-selected values before its existing PUT.
Implicit restoration still requires the actual temporary binding receipt and the existing server CAS.
No SQL, polling, secret, server endpoint or general recovery framework was added by the journal patch.
journal_review: Only validated id/kind/modelId/provider/chosen are copied from an explicit original model; values are preserved, not normalized.
An implicit original model is represented as preferenceState=absent; the actual binding receipt is recorded only after receipt validation.

Prepared Profile metadata contains id, original version/digest/enabled, acknowledged written version/digest and closed intent/restored status fields. No name, instructions, description, skills or definition body enters the journal.
The required pre-write checkpoint precedes the mutation flags and the associated new configuration request.
An acknowledgement checkpoint failure unwinds through the existing finally blocks. Cleanup checkpoints catch persistence errors and continue already-required recovery.
A checkpoint failure prevents subsequent new work and is reflected in the safe report; callback input is cloned.

persistence_review.default_connection: The CLI passes writeRecoveryJournal as onRecoveryCheckpoint; the existing workflow wrapper starts that CLI.
persistence_review.artifact: The existing always() upload adds only the exact recovery.json path alongside the report and browser receipt; no directory wildcard is added.

limitations: This is source review and byte comparison only. The reviewer did not execute tests or inspect runtime, production or test-run artifacts.
The final test registration count is a static count, not a claim that tests passed.

The journal accepts a conservative ASCII identifier grammar for modelId/provider. Legitimate custom model strings allowed by the broader product API can be refused before the case's configuration writes.
Client persistence and a server mutation are not a single atomic transaction. A lost selection response may leave only an intent; a real implicit binding receipt is never fabricated.
SIGKILL cannot guarantee JavaScript finally cleanup. The last synced local snapshot may predate a received acknowledgement, and a destroyed runner can prevent artifact upload even with always().
The existing explicit model picker and fallback boolean APIs have no CAS; this patch retains their prior compare-before-write boundary.
The fixed recovery path holds one execution snapshot. The initial checkpoint replaces an old same-path snapshot; separate workflow runners and per-run artifacts retain earlier production receipts.
A recovery journal provides evidence for the existing authorized recovery paths. It does not authorize overwriting concurrent changes or create an automatic general recovery engine.

final_candidate.disposition: The concrete shared identifier defect found in v1 is fixed. The reviewed final blobs preserve the journal privacy and recovery guards within the explicitly documented identifier subset.
final_candidate.source_object_boundary: Three immutable source blobs relative to the fixed f346 baseline. No assembled tree, commit, merge result, test execution or production acceptance is approved by this review.
